title: ASUS warns of critical hard-coded key flaw in Control Center Express
content_md: ASUS released Control Center Express v1.7.29 to fix three critical vulnerabilities that could let remote attackers gain administrative control of the management console and the devices it manages. Of the three, one is a maximum-severity vulnerability (CVSS score: 10.0) tracked under CVE-2026-114202 , arising from a hard-coded cryptographic key used in the product. The flaw lets an unauthenticated remote attacker forge an authentication token and gain administrator privileges, without requiring any privileges or user interaction. The second flaw is CVE-2026-114204 , also a hard-coded key problem, which lets a remote attacker with low privileges forge a session token for a recently logged-in account. The third is CVE-2026-114205 , an authorization flaw that lets a low-privileged user create an administrator account. ASUS Control Center Express is a central dashboard that IT administrators use to monitor and remotely manage fleets of PCs. ASUS markets it to businesses and IT service providers and lists support for more than 200 of its business, workstation, and Corporate Stable Model motherboards. While all three vulnerabilities are rated critical, CVE-2026-114204 has a recent-session prerequisite, and CVE-2026-114205 requires a low-privileged account, whereas CVE-2026-114202 enables remote administrative access with no prerequisites.
